key_provisions: GenAI users must include a bold verification in their pleadings.
The verification lists programs used and whether used for work product, research, or drafting.
The verification certifies no misstatements, improper citations, confidential information, or AI-created evidence.
summary: Judge Santini’s 457th District Court order requires any attorney or self-represented litigant using generative AI in work product, research, or drafting to include a bold verification in pleadings. The order also prohibits sensitive inputs, AI-created or altered evidence, AI-reliant interpreters, and AI-reliant expert methodology.
text_excerpt: "must include the following verification in bold in their pleadings"
title: 457th District Court Standing Order on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

court: 284th District Court of Montgomery County
key_provisions: GenAI users must include a bold verification in pleadings.
The verification discloses programs used and the role of AI in work product, research, or drafting.
The order prohibits sensitive information, AI-created evidence, AI voice-translation interpreters, and AI-reliant expert methodology.
summary: Judge Bays’s 284th District Court order mirrors the Montgomery County generative-AI verification format. Pleadings using generative AI must include a bold verification listing the AI program and use, certifying accuracy and confidentiality, and confirming no AI-created, edited, enhanced, or altered evidence is attached.
text_excerpt: "I have used ... (list Generative AI programs used) in either my work product, research, and/or drafting of this pleading"
title: 284th District Court Standing Order on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

court: 25th and 2nd 25th District Courts of Texas
judge: Judge William D. Old III; Judge Jessica Crawford
key_provisions: GenAI users must include a bold verification in pleadings.
The verification identifies the programs used and how they were used.
The order prohibits confidential inputs, AI-created evidence, AI voice-translation interpreters, and AI-reliant experts.
sanctions_language: "including but not limited to death penalty sanctions"
summary: The 25th and 2nd 25th District Courts’ generative-AI order requires AI users to include a bold pleading verification listing programs used and describing the use for work product, research, or drafting. It also imposes confidentiality protections and prohibits AI-created evidence, AI-reliant interpreters, and AI-reliant expert opinions.
text_excerpt: "I have used ... (list Generative AI programs used) in either my work product, research, and/or drafting of this pleading"
title: 25th and 2nd 25th District Courts Standing Order on Use of Generative AI

court: Williamson County District Courts and County Courts at Law
key_provisions: AI users must ensure AI-generated information is accurate and correctly portrayed.
A Certificate Regarding Use of Artificial Intelligence must be attached to any filing where AI-generated information is used.
The certificate requires traditional-source verification of AI-created legal content.
sanctions_language: "could subject a party to the court’s inherent power to sanction"
summary: Williamson County local rules contain a dedicated AI-in-filings section. Attorneys and self-represented litigants using AI for legal research or drafting must ensure AI-generated information is accurate and must attach a certificate to any filing where AI-generated information is used.
text_excerpt: "shall sign and submit the Certificate Regarding Use of Artificial Intelligence ... and attach it to any filing where AI-generated information is used"
title: Williamson County Local Rules: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings

court: Grayson County District Courts and County Courts at Law
key_provisions: AI users must attach a certificate to each pleading generated using AI.
The certificate requires traditional-source verification by a human being.
Artificial intelligence for recording, listening, or transcribing in courtrooms and court offices is strictly prohibited.
summary: Grayson County’s local rules include an AI certificate and courtroom prohibition. Filers using AI for legal research or drafting must attach a certificate to AI-generated pleadings, verifying language, citations, arguments, and analysis through traditional legal sources, and AI recording or transcription in court areas is strictly prohibited.
text_excerpt: "sign and submit an attachment to each pleading generated using artificial intelligence"
title: Grayson County Local Rules on Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings

court: Collin County District Courts
key_provisions: AI users must ensure AI-generated information is accurate and correctly portrayed to the court.
The rule covers legal research or drafting in connection with a case.
No separate disclosure or certificate appears in the AI rule text.
summary: Collin County District Courts’ 2026 local rules include a short AI-in-filings rule. Attorneys and self-represented litigants using AI for legal research or drafting must ensure that AI-generated information used in a court submission or proceeding is accurate and correctly portrayed to the court.
text_excerpt: "shall, before using any AI-generated information in a court submission or proceeding, ensure that such information is accurate and correctly portrayed to the court"
title: Collin County District Courts Local Rules: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings

court: Hays County Courts at Law
key_provisions: AI users must certify in writing before filing or presenting AI-generated information.
The certification covers all information created or contributed by GenAI.
Verification must be through traditional non-AI legal sources.
summary: Hays County Courts at Law Local Rule 1.07 requires attorneys and self-represented litigants using AI for legal research or drafting to certify in writing before filing or presenting AI-generated information. The certification covers language, quotations, sources, citations, arguments, and legal analysis verified through traditional legal sources.
text_excerpt: "shall, before filing or presenting to a Court any AI-generated information ... certify in writing"
title: Hays County Courts at Law Local Rule 1.07 Certification Regarding Use of Artificial Intelligence

court: Bexar County Civil District Courts
key_provisions: All pleadings must include an AI certificate on the court-approved form.
The certificate attests that generative-AI-produced legal content will be verified before submission.
Verification must be by Texas-licensed or admitted counsel or by a self-represented litigant through traditional non-AI sources.
summary: Bexar County Civil District Courts’ local rules require all pleadings to include an approved AI certification. The certificate attests that drafted language, quotations, sources, citations, arguments, and legal analyses produced by generative AI will be verified before submission through traditional legal sources.
text_excerpt: "All pleadings shall include a certificate ... attesting that ... legal analyses produced by generative A.I. will—before submission—be verified"
title: Bexar County Civil District Courts Local Rules A.I. Certification

court: Tarrant County Criminal Courts
key_provisions: All motions and briefs must certify whether they were created using AI.
If AI was used, the certification must say all drafted language, citations, arguments, and analyses were verified by a human.
On request, the filer must disclose specific AI-created parts and the AI name.
summary: Tarrant County Criminal Local Rule 5.33 defines AI broadly and requires every motion and brief to include a certification saying whether AI was used. If AI was used, the filer must certify human verification of AI-created content, and the court may request the specific AI-created parts and AI name.
text_excerpt: "All motions and briefs filed with the court shall include a certification ... attesting either that the document was created using A.I. or ... not created using A.I."
title: Tarrant County Criminal Local Rule 5.33: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings

court: Lubbock County District Courts and County Courts at Law
key_provisions: Family standing order includes a short AI liability section.
All attorneys and self-represented litigants remain responsible for filing accuracy.
Reliance on AI-generated fabricated citations or facts may result in sanctions.
summary: Lubbock County’s standing order regarding children, property, and conduct of parties includes an AI liability provision. It does not require disclosure or certification, but it warns attorneys and self-represented litigants that they remain responsible for filing accuracy and may be sanctioned for AI-generated false citations or facts.
text_excerpt: "Reliance on AI-generated information that results in the submission of fabricated, misleading, or non-existent citations or facts may result in sanctions"
title: Lubbock County Standing Order Regarding Children, Property, Conduct, and AI Liability

court: Texas Business Court
key_provisions: The local rule states AI use is not prohibited.
The filing attorney or party is independently responsible for accuracy of all filings.
Filers must comply with legal and ethical duties, including Texas Rule 13 and Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapters 9-10.
summary: Texas Business Court Local Rule 10(c), as posted through TOPICs, expressly says use of artificial intelligence is not prohibited. It imposes no separate disclosure or certificate, but it states that the filing attorney or party remains independently responsible for accuracy and existing legal and ethical duties.
text_excerpt: "Use of artificial intelligence is not prohibited, but the filing attorney or party is independently responsible for the accuracy of all filings"
title: Texas Business Court Local Rule 10(c): Artificial Intelligence

court: Texas Business Court, First Division
key_provisions: Judge Whitehill’s guidelines state AI notetakers may not join virtual conferences.
The restriction appears in the Early Management and Accessibility section.
The guidelines otherwise direct parties to follow Texas Business Court local rules.
summary: Judge Whitehill’s Texas Business Court Division 1B guidelines include a specific AI notetaker rule. The guidelines do not regulate AI drafting of filings, but they prohibit AI notetakers from joining virtual conferences, functioning as a judge-specific courtroom or proceeding access rule.
text_excerpt: "The court does not allow AI notetakers to join virtual conferences."
title: Judge Whitehill Guidelines: AI Notetakers
